tools.name: get_import_format
tools.description: The JSON format for maps: layers with timed polygon keyframes, point markers and a style.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: The signed-in user's public handle, plan and how many maps they can still create.

tools.name: list_maps
tools.description: The user's maps, most recently changed first, with their ids and links.

tools.name: get_map
tools.description: A summary of one of the user's maps (layers, keyframe dates, markers) and a 15-minute download link for its full import JSON, which can be several MB.

tools.name: create_map
tools.description: Create a new private draft map from an import JSON of up to about 1 MB.

tools.name: create_upload_link
tools.description: A one-off link (valid 15 minutes) for uploading a map JSON file of up to 40 MB with curl. It creates a new draft map, or with mode replace overwrites an existing map's content. The curl output reports the result.

tools.name: start_map_upload
tools.description: Opens an upload (valid 2 hours) for a map JSON text that is sent in numbered parts through tool calls rather than over the network. It creates a new draft map, or with mode replace overwrites an existing map's content.

tools.name: upload_map_part
tools.description: Stores one numbered piece of a chunked map upload. The pieces are joined in part order with nothing in between; sending a part number again replaces that part. Returns the piece's length and SHA-256.

tools.name: finish_map_upload
tools.description: Joins parts 1 to the given count of a chunked upload, validates the map and creates the draft map (or replaces the map's content, keeping a backup). Reports missing parts or where the JSON breaks.

tools.name: replace_map_content
tools.description: Overwrite an existing map's layers, markers, name, description and casualty bar (and style, if given) with an import JSON of up to about 1 MB. The link and publish state stay; the old content is backed up.

tools.name: publish_map
tools.description: Make one of the user's maps public at its /map/<handle>/<slug> link, where anyone can view it. The user must first choose a username at https://www.movingpolygons.com/settings; until then this fails and says so.

tools.name: unpublish_map
tools.description: Make one of the user's maps private again (its public link stops working).

tools.name: search_maps
tools.description: Find published animated maps on Moving Polygons (history, wars, empires, borders, epidemics, sea ice…) by words in their title or description and/or a year they cover. Returns links to the interactive map, its text version and its article.

tools.name: get_public_map
tools.description: One published map as Markdown: description and sources, the timeline of keyframes (date and caption), layers, events, and the iframe code to embed the interactive map. Pass its URL, or the handle and slug.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_public_map · Private data: create_map, create_upload_link, unpublish_map · Public sink: create_upload_link, start_map_upload, upload_map_part, finish_map_upload, replace_map_content, publish_map · Destructive: get_import_format, replace_map_content.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_public_map · Private data: create_map, create_upload_link, unpublish_map · Public sink: create_upload_link, start_map_upload, upload_map_part, finish_map_upload, replace_map_content, publish_map · Destructive: get_import_format, replace_map_content

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "publish_map" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Make one of the user's maps public at its /map/<handle>/<slug> link, where anyone can view it." → after: "Make one of the user's maps public at its /map/<handle>/<slug> link, where anyone can view it. The user must first choose a username at https://www.movingpolygons.com/settings; until then this fails and says so."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
